> Long-form companion to `@sec-debias-general` of the methods note. The aim is the full
> mathematical statement of the condition under which León's (2024) bootstrap de-biasing and
> infinitesimal-jackknife (IJ) variance can be expressed via the fast multiplier (wild /
> martingale) bootstrap for a *general* subgroup-identification procedure, with a worked
> logistic / log-odds-ratio example. We will condense this for the main paper.

# Setup and notation {#sec-setup}

Let $O_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)$, $i=1,\dots,N$, with treatment $A_i\in\{0,1\}$, covariates $X_i$, and
outcome $Y_i$ (with a censoring indicator in the survival case). A candidate family
$\mathcal F=\{g_1,\dots,g_S\}$ indexes subgroups $g\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}$ defined by covariate
conjunctions.

**Inferential estimand.** For subgroup $g$ the target is the *within-subgroup treatment effect*
$\beta(g)$ on the natural-parameter scale — the coefficient on $A$ in a Cox or GLM model fit to
$\{i\in g\}$. The estimator $\hat\beta(g)$ solves the within-subgroup score equation
$$
U_g(\beta)\;:=\;\sum_{i\in g}\psi_i(\beta;g)\;=\;0,
$$ {#eq-score}
where $\psi_i$ is the per-subject score contribution (Cox partial-likelihood score / GLM score).

**Influence (dfbeta).** With within-subgroup information
$\mathcal I_g=-\partial U_g/\partial\beta\big|_{\hat\beta(g)}$, the empirical influence of subject
$i$ on $\hat\beta(g)$ is the dfbeta
$$
\mathrm{db}_{g,i}\;=\;\mathcal I_g^{-1}\,\psi_i\!\big(\hat\beta(g);g\big),\qquad i\in g,
\qquad \sum_{i\in g}\mathrm{db}_{g,i}=0,
$$ {#eq-dfbeta}
the last equality because the scores sum to zero at $\hat\beta(g)$.

**Multiplier / bootstrap perturbation.** A resample $b$ assigns subject $i$ a multiplicity
$K^{*}_{bi}$ ($\sum_i K^{*}_{bi}=N$). The reweighted estimator satisfies, to first order,
$$
\hat\beta^{*}_b(g)-\hat\beta(g)
=\sum_{i\in g}\big(K^{*}_{bi}-1\big)\,\mathrm{db}_{g,i}+o_p(1)
\;=:\;D_g(b).
$$ {#eq-perturb}
Collect the centered multiplicities $G_i(b)=K^{*}_{bi}-1$ in $\boldsymbol\Xi\in\mathbb R^{N\times B}$
and the effect influences in $\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}}\in\mathbb R^{N\times S}$,
$(\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}})_{ig}=\mathrm{db}_{g,i}\,\mathbf 1\{i\in g\}$. Then
$D_g(b)=(\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\top}\boldsymbol\Xi)_{gb}=:P_{gb}$, and with centered-Poisson
weights $G_i(b)\to\mathrm{Poisson}(1)-1$ this is the infinitesimal-jackknife linearization of the
nonparametric bootstrap [@efron2014].

# The selection map and León's correction {#sec-leon}

A subgroup-identification procedure returns $\widehat H\in\mathcal F$ by applying a rule
$\mathcal S$ to a vector of per-candidate **selection statistics** $\mathbf S=(S_1,\dots,S_S)$:
$$
\widehat H=\mathcal S(\mathbf S),\qquad S_g=\text{the statistic the procedure ranks on}.
$$ {#eq-selmap}
León's [@leon2024] bias-corrected estimator of the *inferential effect* (their Eq. 7) is
$$
\tilde\beta(\widehat H)=\hat\beta(\widehat H)-\frac1B\sum_{b=1}^{B}
\Big[\underbrace{\eta^{*}_b(\widehat H^{*}_b)}_{\text{selection optimism}}
+\underbrace{\eta^{*}_b(\widehat H)}_{\text{estimation bias at }\widehat H}\Big],
\qquad \eta^{*}_b(g)=\hat\beta^{*}_b(g)-\hat\beta(g),
$$ {#eq-leon7}
where $\widehat H^{*}_b=\mathcal S(\mathbf S^{*}_b)$ is the procedure's selection on resample $b$.
Two facts must hold *simultaneously*:

1. The bias terms $\eta^{*}_b(g)$ are **effect** discrepancies — because the target is
   $\hat\beta(\widehat H)$ — so by @eq-perturb $\eta^{*}_b(g)=D_g(b)$, governed by
   $\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
2. The re-selected winner $\widehat H^{*}_b$ is governed by the **procedure's** statistic
   $\mathbf S^{*}_b$, which need not be the effect.

**Decomposition.** The first term of @eq-leon7 averages the effect discrepancy at the
*re-selected* subgroup; since $\widehat H^{*}_b$ is re-chosen each resample (mimicking the
original selection), it captures **selection optimism** — the winner's curse, and exactly the
Harrell–Lee–Mark [@harrell1996] optimism term. The second term averages the effect discrepancy
at the *fixed observed* subgroup (no re-selection); it is the bootstrap estimate of the
**estimation bias** of $\hat\beta$ at $\widehat H$ — the estimator's own finite-sample bias —
which Harrell's correction omits and León retains. (Under the linearization @eq-perturb,
$\mathbb E^{*}D_{\widehat H}=0$, so the second term is mean-zero to leading order; its $O(1/n)$
content is the estimation bias, and it carries the per-draw residual of the IJ variance,
@sec-ij.)

# The Tier-2 linearization and the selection statistic {#sec-tier2}

Tier-2 replaces the per-resample refits by influence arithmetic on two fronts:

* **(a) the bias magnitude:** $\eta^{*}_b(g)\approx D_g(b)$, from the *effect* influences
  $\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}}$;
* **(b) the re-selection:** $\widehat H^{*}_b\approx\mathcal S(\hat{\mathbf S}_b)$, from the
  linearized *selection* statistics.

For (b) we must linearize the procedure's *own* statistic. Let $\mathrm{dt}_{g,i}$ be the
influence of subject $i$ on $S_g$, and
$$
S^{*}_{b,g}-S_g=E_g(b)+o_p(1),\qquad
E_g(b)=\sum_i\big(K^{*}_{bi}-1\big)\,\mathrm{dt}_{g,i},
$$ {#eq-Eperturb}
so $\widehat H^{*}_b\approx\mathcal S(\{S_g+E_g(b)\}_g)$. The selection-bias term of @eq-leon7
becomes
$$
\boxed{\;\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}
=\frac1B\sum_{b}D_{\widehat H^{*}_b}(b)
=\frac1B\sum_{b}D_{\,\mathcal S(\{S_g+E_g(b)\})}(b).\;}
$$ {#eq-key}
This is the *effect* perturbation $D$ evaluated at the winner of the *statistic* competition.
**Two influence systems are entangled:** $E$ (statistic, via $\mathrm{dt}$) decides *which*
candidate wins; $D$ (effect, via $\mathrm{db}$) decides the magnitude *credited*. They share the
multipliers $\boldsymbol\Xi$ (one resample), so $D$ and $E$ are jointly dependent.

# Effect selection vs native selection {#sec-cases}

## Case A — effect selection (`select_statistic = "effect"`)

The procedure ranks on the inferential effect: $S_g=\hat\beta(g)$, hence
$\mathrm{dt}_{g,i}=\mathrm{db}_{g,i}$ and $E_g(b)=D_g(b)$. @eq-key becomes
$$
\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}
=\frac1B\sum_b D_{\,\arg\max_g(\hat\beta(g)+D_g(b))}(b).
$$ {#eq-biasA}
Conditional on $g$ winning, $\hat\beta(g)+D_g(b)$ is maximal, so $D_g(b)$ is an *upper-tail order
statistic* of $\{D_{g'}(b)\}$: $\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}>0$ and it equals exactly
the optimism of effect-ranking selection — the quantity León's Eq. 7 corrects, computed from
$\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}}$ alone. The gate's re-selection
$\mathcal S(\{\hat\beta(g)+D_g(b)\})$ *is* the linearized procedure. **Faithful.**

## Case B — native selection (DINA / GRF / Lasso)

The procedure ranks on $S_g=T_g\neq\hat\beta(g)$ with $E_g(b)\neq D_g(b)$. The native bootstrap
re-selects on $T+E$:
$$
\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}^{\text{native}}
=\frac1B\sum_b D_{\,\arg\max_g(T_g+E_g(b))}(b).
$$ {#eq-biasBnative}
An effect-based gate that re-selects on $\hat\beta+D$ instead computes
$$
\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}^{\text{gate}}
=\frac1B\sum_b D_{\,\arg\max_g(\hat\beta(g)+D_g(b))}(b)
\;\neq\;\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}^{\text{native}},
$$ {#eq-biasBgate}
because $\arg\max_g(T_g+E_g(b))\neq\arg\max_g(\hat\beta(g)+D_g(b))$ on any draw where the
*statistic* ordering and the *effect* ordering disagree. The gate estimates the optimism of an
effect-ranking procedure **that was never run**; the actual (native) procedure has a different —
generally smaller — effect optimism. So an effect-based gate **mis-corrects** a native-ranking
procedure.

**What faithful native de-biasing would require.** To linearize a native-ranked procedure one
needs: (i) the native influences $\mathrm{dt}_{g,i}$; (ii) the *joint* perturbations
$(D_g(b),E_g(b))$ under shared $\boldsymbol\Xi$; (iii) re-selection on $T+E$ with the bias read
from $D$ via @eq-key; and (iv) the IJ variance from the joint law. This is a strictly heavier
construction — **two** influence matrices $\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}},\mathbf B_{\mathrm{nat}}$ and
their cross-covariance. Setting $S_g=\hat\beta(g)$ collapses (i)–(iv) to a single influence
matrix and the gate is exact.

::: {.callout-important}
**Proposition (alignment).** The Tier-2 de-biased estimator @eq-leon7 and its IJ interval
(@sec-ij) reproduce León's bootstrap to first order for a procedure with selection map
$\mathcal S$ **iff** the procedure ranks on the inferential effect, $S_g=\hat\beta(g)$
(equivalently, iff $\mathcal S(\{\hat\beta(g)+D_g(b)\})$ equals the procedure's linearized
bootstrap re-selection). Re-ranking a native procedure's *qualifying candidates* on
$\hat\beta(g)$ enforces the condition by construction, at the cost of demoting the native model
to a candidate generator.
:::

# The native statistics, explicitly {#sec-natstat}

**DINA** [@gao2025]. The per-patient effect is $\hat\tau_i=a_i^{\top}\hat\beta_{\mathrm D}$, with
$\hat\beta_{\mathrm D}$ the cross-fit natural-parameter coefficient vector and $a_i$ the contrast
row. The native statistic is the subgroup mean
$$
T_g=\frac1{|g|}\sum_{i\in g}\hat\tau_i
=\Big(\tfrac1{|g|}\textstyle\sum_{i\in g}a_i\Big)^{\!\top}\hat\beta_{\mathrm D}
=\bar a_g^{\top}\hat\beta_{\mathrm D},
$$ {#eq-dinaT}
whose resampling perturbation is
$$
E_g(b)=\bar a_g^{\top}\big(\hat\beta^{*}_{\mathrm D,b}-\hat\beta_{\mathrm D}\big)
=\sum_i\big(K^{*}_{bi}-1\big)\,\underbrace{\bar a_g^{\top}\,\mathrm{IF}_{\mathrm D}(O_i)}_{\textstyle \mathrm{dt}_{g,i}},
$$ {#eq-dinaE}
with $\mathrm{IF}_{\mathrm D}$ the influence function of the **global** DINA fit. Contrast this
with the **local** effect influence $\mathrm{db}_{g,i}=\mathcal I_g^{-1}\psi_i(\hat\beta(g);g)$ of
@eq-dfbeta: $\mathrm{dt}_{g,i}$ is a global-fit influence weighted by the subgroup-mean contrast
$\bar a_g$, whereas $\mathrm{db}_{g,i}$ is a within-subgroup M-estimator influence. In general
$\bar a_g^{\top}\mathrm{IF}_{\mathrm D}(O_i)\neq\mathcal I_g^{-1}\psi_i(\hat\beta(g);g)$, so
$E_g(b)\neq D_g(b)$.

A sharper point: even if the *point* statistics happened to coincide, $T_g=\hat\beta(g)$ for all
$g$, the *perturbations* would still generally differ ($E_g(b)\neq D_g(b)$) because the influence
functions differ. The per-draw re-selection — and hence @eq-key — would still mismatch.
**Alignment must be enforced at the level of the statistic the gate perturbs:** the procedure
must *select on* $\hat\beta(g)$, not merely have a native statistic numerically close to it.

**GRF** [@wagerathey2018; @atheytibshiraniwager2019]. The native statistic is a subgroup mean of
doubly-robust scores, $T_g=\tfrac1{|g|}\sum_{i\in g}\hat\Gamma_i$, with $\hat\Gamma_i$ the AIPW
pseudo-outcome from the forest's nuisance estimates; $\mathrm{dt}_{g,i}$ then involves the
influence of $\hat\Gamma_i$ — again distinct from $\mathrm{db}_{g,i}$.

**Lasso.** A penalized rule selects variables along the regularization path; its "statistic" is
the penalized coefficient ordering, whose perturbation is governed by the path's influence, not
the within-subgroup effect's. Same alignment requirement.

# Worked example: logistic / log-odds-ratio, two candidates {#sec-example}

Take a binary outcome with treatment effect on the log-odds-ratio scale, and two overlapping
candidate subgroups $g_1,g_2$. Suppose on the observed data:

| quantity | $g_1$ | $g_2$ | ranks |
|---|---|---|---|
| within-subgroup log-OR $\hat\beta(g)$ | $0.90$ | $1.00$ | **effect:** $g_2\succ g_1$ |
| DINA subgroup-mean $T_g=\overline{\hat\tau}_g$ | $0.55$ | $0.50$ | **native:** $g_1\succ g_2$ |

The divergence is realistic: $g_1$ may contain a concentrated high-$\hat\tau$ region that lifts
its *mean* individual effect, while $g_2$'s larger *within-group* odds ratio comes with more
dilution — a covariate-weighted average of individual effects ($T_g$) and the within-group
contrast ($\hat\beta(g)$) need not co-rank.

**Procedure run = DINA (native):** $\widehat H=g_1$ (largest $T_g$).

Consider one resample $b$ whose multipliers produce
$$
D_{g_1}(b)=+0.05,\quad D_{g_2}(b)=+0.30,\qquad
E_{g_1}(b)=+0.12,\quad E_{g_2}(b)=+0.02,
$$
i.e. this draw inflates $g_2$'s *effect* the most but $g_1$'s *native statistic* the most (the
two influence systems point different ways — exactly the entanglement of @eq-key).

| re-selection rule | compares | winner | effect credited $D_{\widehat H^{*}_b}(b)$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **native** (what DINA's bootstrap does) | $T_1{+}E_1=0.67$ vs $T_2{+}E_2=0.52$ | $g_1$ | $D_{g_1}(b)=\mathbf{+0.05}$ |
| **effect gate** (re-selects on $\hat\beta{+}D$) | $\hat\beta_1{+}D_1=0.95$ vs $\hat\beta_2{+}D_2=1.30$ | $g_2$ | $D_{g_2}(b)=\mathbf{+0.30}$ |

On this single draw the native bootstrap credits $+0.05$ to $\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}$,
the effect gate credits $+0.30$. Averaged over draws,
$\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}^{\text{gate}}\gg
\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}^{\text{native}}$: the effect gate **over-states** the
selection optimism of the procedure that was actually run, and would **over-shrink**
$\hat\beta(g_1)=0.90$ toward the null. The mis-correction is precisely the gap between "optimism
of effect-ranking" and "optimism of $\hat\tau$-ranking."

**Under `select_statistic = "effect"`** the procedure instead selects $\widehat H=g_2$ (the
effect winner on the observed data), and the gate's re-selection is the faithful linearization of
*that* procedure: $\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}$ is the effect-ranking optimism,
correctly removed. The reported subgroup is now the effect-defined one ($g_2$), and its de-biased
estimate and IJ interval are first-order exact **conditional on $\{g_1,g_2\}$**.

# The interval, under alignment {#sec-ij}

With $S_g=\hat\beta(g)$ (so $E\equiv D$), the IJ variance of the bagged estimator @eq-leon7
[@efron2014; @wagerhastie2014] is read from the same draws. With row-centered multipliers
$\tilde G_i(b)=G_i(b)-\bar G_i$ and per-draw residual
$$
r_b=\big(\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{sel}}+\widehat{\mathrm{bias}}_{\mathrm{fix}}\big)
-D_{\widehat H^{*}_b}(b)-D_{\widehat H}(b),
$$
$$
\widetilde{\mathrm{cov}}_i=\frac1B\sum_b\tilde G_i(b)\,r_b,\qquad
\tilde V=\sum_i\widetilde{\mathrm{cov}}_i^{\,2},\qquad
\hat V=\tilde V-\frac NB\,\frac1B\sum_b r_b^2,
$$ {#eq-ij}
and the de-biased interval is $\tilde\beta(\widehat H)\pm z\sqrt{\hat V}$ (exponentiated for
ratios). Under *native* selection the residual and the re-selection would each require $E$, and
the variance the *joint* law of $(D,E)$ — the same two-influence-matrix obstruction as the point
estimate. Alignment closes the interval on $\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eff}}$ alone.

# Scope: conditional on the family {#sec-scope}

The development above fixes the candidate family $\mathcal F$. For an enumerated family (forest
search) a bootstrap re-selects over the same $\mathcal F$, so the fixed-family Tier-2 computation
is faithful. For DINA/GRF, $\mathcal F$ is itself produced by the cross-fit surface / forest and
would regenerate to $\mathcal F^{*}_b$ on a resample. The fast gate enumerates the observed-data
family (banded to the effect neighbourhood) and so targets the estimand **conditional on the
proposed family**:
$$
\beta\big(\widehat H\big),\quad
\widehat H=\arg\max_{g\in\mathcal F}\hat\beta(g)\ \text{(per the rule)},\ \mathcal F\ \text{given.}
$$
Under this conditional target, with alignment, @eq-leon7 and @eq-ij are first-order exact. The
*unconditional* target additionally bootstraps $\mathcal F$; the fast gate then omits the
family-generation component of both the bias and the variance, an omission that vanishes when
$\mathcal F$ approaches the full space and grows when $\mathcal F$ is a tight, surface-selected
handful — to be quantified against a literal Tier-1 that regenerates the family.

# Summary {#sec-summary}

The bias León corrects is an *effect* discrepancy (@eq-leon7), so the bootstrap re-selection it
averages over (@eq-key) must be governed by the effect. A procedure that ranks on a *different*
statistic re-selects different winners on the same resample (@eq-biasBnative vs @eq-biasBgate),
averaging the optimism over the wrong distribution; the worked example (@sec-example) shows the
per-draw winner flip explicitly. Re-ranking the procedure's qualifying candidates on
$\hat\beta(g)$ (`select_statistic = "effect"`) makes the selection a functional of the effects,
collapses the two influence systems into one, and renders the fast de-biasing and IJ interval
first-order exact — **conditional on the proposed family**. This is the precise sense in which
the resampling paradigm is "procedure-agnostic," and the precise way it constrains model-based
selectors such as DINA, GRF, and Lasso.
